Definition: probably from G142 (perhaps with G1 (as a particle of union) prefixed); a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare G719)):--chariot.
BiblicalUsage: A chariot was the fastest seat in the ancient world, and the New Testament puts two very different riders in one. In Acts 8:28 the Ethiopian eunuch sits in his chariot reading Isaiah, in Acts 8:29 the Spirit tells Philip to go near it, and in Acts 8:38 they stop the chariot and Philip baptizes him. Revelation 9:9 turns the picture dark, with locusts whose wings sound like many chariots running to battle.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the chariot shows me both ends of the gospel: a seeking man reading the prophet on the road, and the judgment that comes for those who will not listen. Philip ran to the one, and the other is still coming.
